summary: Show several people or identities as one compact visual cue.

useWhen.text: Show several people or identities as one compact visual cue.

from.quote: Show several people or identities as one compact visual cue.

useWhen.text: Show who can access a shared account.

from.quote: Show who can access a shared account

anatomy.holds: It starts at the back of the visual order and gives the group its first face.

from.quote: It starts at the back of the visual order and gives the group its first face.

anatomy.holds: It overlaps the first child and sits behind the last.

from.quote: It overlaps the first child and sits behind the last.

anatomy.holds: The final child is drawn in front. Child order therefore changes which face leads.

from.quote: The final child is drawn in front. Child order therefore changes which face leads.

placementAdvice.text: Give the host room for every child: the row grows with its child count.

from.quote: The row grows with its child count.

placementAdvice.text: A narrower host doesn't shrink the Avatars: select a supported Avatar Size that fits (the guide fits four children at M in a 196 px host and at S in a 112 px host).

from.quote: A narrower host does not reduce Avatar Size automatically, so select a supported size that fits.

placementAdvice.text: Don't overfill a fixed-width host: a row with more children than fit extends past it, and the guide's host clips the outer Avatars.

from.quote: This five-child row extends past both edges, so the host clips its outer Avatars.

placementAdvice.text: A Coin Card can wrap a title, support text and the AvatarGroup in one composition; the Card adds that optional context outside the group.

from.quote: A public Coin Card can wrap its title, support text, and AvatarGroup in one composition.

configuration.text: Avatar Size belongs to the group: set it once on the AvatarGroup, and the group gives that one size to every child.

from.quote: Avatar Size belongs to the group mode.

configuration.text: Share one size across the Avatar children.

from.quote: Share one size across the Avatar children.

configuration.text: Don't set Avatar Size on a child: a child's own mode takes precedence over the group's, so that child comes out a different size from the others.

from.quote: An explicit L child mode takes precedence over the group’s M mode.

configuration.text: With no Avatar Size set, the group and its children are L (42 px).
Avatar Size L, M, S and XS make every child 42, 36, 29 or 14 px.

from.quote: Figma’s Avatar Size mode sets L/M/S/XS to 42/36/29/14 px.

configuration.text: There is no separate count or gap control: the children supply the members and their image or monogram.

from.quote: The children supply the image or monogram; there is no separate count or gap control.

configuration.text: AvatarGroup adds no selected, disabled or loading state of its own: loading belongs to each Avatar child.

from.quote: Avatar Group does not add a selected, disabled, or loading state.

rules.text: Use Avatar children: the group's content is the Avatar instances supplied inside it.

from.quote: The group’s content is the Avatar instances supplied inside it.

rules.text: The group itself contains only its Avatar children; a title or support text stays outside it, for example in a surrounding Card.

from.quote: The group itself contains only its Avatar children.

rules.text: Each child supplies its own image or monogram content.

from.quote: Each child supplies its own image or monogram content.

rules.text: Order the children intentionally: the last child sits in front, so child order changes which face leads.

from.quote: The last child sits in front in the overlapping group.

rules.text: For an Image child, supply that person's own imageSource: with none, the Avatar shows a bundled fallback image, which is not a person record.

from.quote: With no `imageSource`, the implementation displays a bundled fallback image; use a supplied person-specific source for identity rather than treating the fallback as a person record.

states.when: The group stays a compact composition of the children it receives.

from.quote: The group stays a compact composition of the children it receives.

states.when: One Avatar child is loading: it shows a same-size skeleton while the other Avatar children remain visible.

from.quote: The loading child shows a same-size skeleton while the other Avatar children remain visible.

accessibility.text: Don't rely on the Avatar children to announce who is in the group: Avatar discards its accessibility label and hides its image and initials from accessibility.

from.quote: The guides do not present it as an accessible action or rely on Avatar to announce its content.

doDont.why: An explicit L child mode takes precedence over the group’s M mode.

from.quote: All three children inherit M from AvatarGroup.

doDont.why: This five-child row extends past both edges, so the host clips its outer Avatars.

from.quote: All three circles stay inside the visible 112 px host.

examples.purpose: Who can view a shared account, the guide's In context: a Card wraps the title, the support text and the AvatarGroup, and the group holds only its three Monogram Avatars. The size, M (36 px), is set once on the group: it is what the guide's In context card draws in its code (its copy names no size), and what its Do & Don't's three children inherit. The Avatars set no size of their own.
examples.jsx:
<Card variant="slim">
  <HStack alignVertical="center" justifyHorizontal="space-between">
    <VStack>
      <Card.Title>Shared savings</Card.Title>
      <Card.SupportText>People who can view this account</Card.SupportText>
    </VStack>
    <AvatarGroup modes={{ 'Avatar Size': 'M' }}>
      <Avatar style="Monogram" monogram="MS" />
      <Avatar style="Monogram" monogram="AK" />
      <Avatar style="Monogram" monogram="LS" />
    </AvatarGroup>
  </HStack>
</Card>

from.quote: A public Coin Card can wrap its title, support text, and AvatarGroup in one composition.

examples.purpose: Two people at the default size, L (42 px), with no modes set: the group gives both one size, and each Avatar brings its own content, a person's own photo (the Image style, the default; the URI stands for that person's image) or initials.

from.quote: The group mode supplies one size to every child; each Avatar supplies its own image or monogram.

examples.purpose: Four people in a narrow place, like the guide's 112 px host: the group doesn't shrink its Avatars, so select a supported size that fits, here S (29 px), set once on the group.
examples.jsx:
<AvatarGroup modes={{ 'Avatar Size': 'S' }}>
  <Avatar style="Monogram" monogram="MS" />
  <Avatar style="Monogram" monogram="AK" />
  <Avatar style="Monogram" monogram="LS" />
  <Avatar style="Monogram" monogram="DV" />
</AvatarGroup>

from.quote: A narrower host does not reduce Avatar Size automatically, so select a supported size that fits.
